title: Distinct Subsequence Count
statement:
Count how many different ways the characters of a pattern can be picked, in order, from a source string.

Contract
- Both strings are non-null and may be empty; characters compare exactly (case-sensitive).
- A selection is a set of positions in `source`, increasing from left to right, whose characters spell `pattern`. Two selections that use different positions count separately even when they spell the same text.
- An empty `pattern` has exactly one selection (choose nothing); a pattern longer than `source` has none.
- The answer fits in a `long`.

Examples
- `countSubsequences("bagbag", "bag")` returns `4`: the `b`, `a`, `g` can be chosen from positions {0,1,2}, {0,1,5}, {0,4,5} or {3,4,5}.
- `countSubsequences("xyz", "xzy")` returns `0`: `y` comes before `z` in the source.
- `countSubsequences("aaaa", "aa")` returns `6`: any two of the four positions.
hints: Whether the pattern's last character is matched by the source's last character splits the count into two disjoint cases.

Let ways[i][j] be the number of ways the first j pattern characters appear in the first i source characters. Always add ways[i - 1][j] (skip source[i]); if the characters match, also add ways[i - 1][j - 1].

Row i only reads row i - 1, so one array works if you update j from high to low. Intended complexity: O(|source| * |pattern|) time and O(|pattern|) extra space; with both strings of length n that is O(n^2) time and O(n) space.
inputSyntax: Input: the source word and the pattern word, for example: bagbag bag
